scope: Broaden primary-source review of open-source DWG/DXF peers and downstream routes; tighten comparison readiness around operation kind and documentation/source/runtime freshness without inferring local defects or support claims.

sourceTypes: LibreDWG upstream NEWS and generated command manual plus GNU manual
ezdxf current xref and drawing add-on documentation
FreeCAD current converter/importer documentation and source
method.sourceFreshnessLimit: Public master/main and stable pages are mutable. Pages are discovery evidence; exact release/commit, local executable/build, and runtime options must be captured together for any differential. The reviewed LibreDWG manual identifies itself as 0.13.4 while upstream NEWS identifies a later 0.14.1 beta, and its generated dwgwrite man page states a narrower writer capability; no behavior was executed here.
method.evidenceRule: A capability statement is scoped to an exact operation, direction, version, class/field, and route. Process success, a project matrix, opaque retention, a geometry projection, and same-codec rewrite are not semantic equivalence or native-application acceptance.

evidence.topic: LibreDWG source, manual, and generated CLI documentation freshness
evidence.observed: The upstream NEWS page identifies 0.14.1 as a 2026-07-25 beta. The generated dwgwrite.1 identifies itself as 0.14 and says ‘Only r2000 for now’ while listing several later --as values. The GNU manual landing page identifies 0.13.4 (2026-03-17); its class chapter distinguishes stable, unstable, debugging, and unhandled classes and warns that some unknown content is downgraded to placeholder-like output unless the full unknown-bit data survives a same-version rewrite.
doesNotEstablish: which later DWG writer target is supported by a particular built LibreDWG executable
that the public manual and generated CLI page describe the same source snapshot
semantic support for every class/version from aggregate coverage language
evidence.planUse: Treat docs/release/source disagreement as a qualification warning. Before using LibreDWG as a writer comparator, pin source or release, capture executable --version/hash/options, request a named target, inspect actual six-byte DWG magic, and reopen independently with per-class/handle disposition. Keep its class stability and unknown-bit policy in comparator metadata.

evidence.topic: ezdxf operation asymmetry: ordinary model support versus xref/copy and rendering
evidence.observed: The current xref docs explicitly exclude ACAD_TABLE and unknown entities represented by DXFTagStorage from supported copy/transform operations and state that unsupported entities are ignored without exceptions. The drawing add-on docs say ACIS rendering is unsupported and there is no 3D rendering engine; 3D entities are projected into the XY plane.
doesNotEstablish: that ordinary parse/save has the same limits as xref/copy
that a successful xref result retained every unsupported source record
ACIS solid or general 3D rendering semantics
that ezdxf's documented limits reveal a matching local libdxfrw defect
evidence.planUse: Make the peer operation mode explicit. A zero exit with no exception is insufficient where documented unsupported records may be silently ignored; capture before/after handle and class disposition. Do not use the ezdxf renderer as a 3D/ACIS acceptance oracle.

evidence.topic: GDAL DXF: raw-carrier exposure is not a DWG reader or solid kernel
evidence.observed: The current driver docs distinguish binary DXF support (GDAL 3.12+) from DWG. The DXF driver normally skips 3DSOLID/REGION/BODY/SURFACE because it cannot create OGR geometry; its optional AC1027+ extensible mode exposes raw ASM data and a 12-value affine transform.
doesNotEstablish: DWG parsing or CAD object-graph preservation
solid reconstruction, ACIS interpretation, or B-rep validity
that a projected OGR feature preserves exact CAD curve/annotation semantics
evidence.planUse: Keep GDAL in the optional DXF syntax/projection/raw-carrier lane. Assert carrier bytes and transform separately, and do not promote raw payload presence into 3D support.

evidence.topic: FreeCAD's DWG path is a multi-stage, configurable consumer pipeline
evidence.observed: Current documentation says native C++ DXF import/export does not implement all DXF features and a legacy Python route remains available; DWG itself is handled by external converters. The DWG adapter creates/uses an intermediate DXF and invokes the DXF importer. The source supports multiple converter choices, so a product-level ‘FreeCAD import’ result does not identify which converter or importer backend ran.
doesNotEstablish: behavior of any particular installed FreeCAD build or platform
which converter/importer preference was active in a given run
complete 3D or ACIS support in the stock importer
that successful conversion to DXF means successful semantic import
evidence.planUse: For native qualification, record FreeCAD build/platform, chosen converter executable/version/options and process outcome, intermediate DXF hash/version, selected C++ or legacy Python importer, preferences, warnings, and final semantic census as separate pipeline stages.

evidence.topic: ACadSharp advertised version matrix remains discovery-only
evidence.observed: The public project page advertises distinct DXF/DWG read/write version matrices and a typed document model.
doesNotEstablish: per-entity and per-field fidelity for each advertised route
graph closure or native application acceptance
the exact commit/release represented by the mutable page
evidence.planUse: Use the matrix only to shortlist route/version probes; bind any actual comparison to a release/commit, build, options, warnings, source/output versions, and feature-level expectations.

addFreshnessFields: peer release or exact source commit
documentation page release/date or retrieval date
runtime executable hash and build options
